# Dashboard keyboard accessibility remediation for audited core flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. It makes each
flow fully operable with keyboard alone and makes focus indicators consistent,
so that keyboard users can complete these flows without pointer input.

## Scope

- Fix the focus-loss defects in modals used by the four audited flows so that
  keyboard focus is retained and returned appropriately when modals open and
  close (no focus traps).
- Make all controls reachable in the four audited flows (no keyboard-unreachable
  controls).
- Apply consistent, visible focus indicators across the audited flows, in line
  with the Dashboard's existing UI conventions.
- Address the per-flow defect list enumerated in the accessibility audit
  report; the audit report is the authoritative defect inventory for this epic.
- Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require,
  and any flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a keyboard-only user, When they navigate the project creation flow from
  entry to completion, Then every step is operable by keyboard alone with no
  focus traps and no unreachable controls.
- Given a keyboard-only user, When they navigate the workbench spawn flow from
  entry to completion, Then every step is operable by keyboard alone with no
  focus traps and no unreachable controls.
- Given a keyboard-only user, When they navigate the model deployment flow from
  entry to completion, Then every step is operable by keyboard alone with no
  focus traps and no unreachable controls.
- Given a keyboard-only user, When they navigate the pipeline run submission
  flow from entry to completion, Then every step is operable by keyboard alone
  with no focus traps and no unreachable controls.
- Given a keyboard user moving focus through controls in the audited flows,
  When an element receives focus, Then a visible focus indicator is shown,
  consistent in style across all four flows.
- Given the audit report's enumerated defects, When the fixes are complete,
  Then each enumerated defect is resolved or explicitly dispositioned.
- Given a pointer user, When the accessibility fixes are in place, Then
  pointer-based operation of the four flows continues to work without
  regression.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with
  no focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by the flow-operability
  acceptance criteria above.
- HLR-2 (P1): Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — covered by the focus-indicator consistency acceptance criterion above.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation —
the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) and the product
documentation's accessibility statement — so that it reflects the fixed state of
the four core Dashboard flows after the keyboard accessibility remediation. Two
public-sector customers require an updated, published conformance statement
before renewal, so the published documentation is a deliverable of equal
standing to the code fixes.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT to reflect the corrected keyboard operability and focus
  indicator conformance of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench
  spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission).
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the fixed
  state.
- Republish both artifacts through the standard documentation publishing
  process.
- Technically review the updated content against the implemented behavior so
  claims in the conformance statement match what was actually built.
- Out of scope: conformance claims for flows or capabilities outside the four
  audited ones, and screen-reader conformance beyond what the keyboard fixes
  establish.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the completed keyboard accessibility remediation of the four audited
  flows, When the VPAT is updated, Then its conformance claims for those flows
  reflect the fixed state and cite the implemented behavior accurately.
- Given the completed remediation, When the product docs accessibility
  statement is updated, Then it reflects the fixed state of the audited flows.
- Given the updated conformance content, When it is reviewed, Then a technical
  review against the implementation confirms accuracy before publication
  (required by HLR-3).
- Given the reviewed content, When publication completes, Then the updated VPAT
  and accessibility statement are publicly available to customers (the
  renewal-blocking deliverable).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P2): The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed
  state, with technical review — covered by all acceptance criteria above.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Strategy: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows

## Triage Outcome

Not triaged as below-threshold or docs-only. Although the code change itself is
small and well-specified (the audit report enumerates the exact defects per
flow), the strategy spans two distinct work streams on two components:

1. **Code implementation** (Dashboard): keyboard operability and focus-indicator
   fixes across the four audited flows.
2. **Substantive content authoring** (Documentation): the VPAT and the product
   docs accessibility statement must be updated and republished — new
   conformance content with technical review, not an incidental touch-up.

Per Step 0 escape condition 2 (code implementation + substantive content
authoring are distinct work streams), the full decomposition applies.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Dashboard keyboard accessibility remediation for audited core flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 Dashboard keyboard accessibility remediation]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 Accessibility conformance documentation]
    E001 --> E002
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | The VPAT and accessibility statement describe the fixed state; they must be authored after the keyboard fixes land and be technically reviewed against the implementation. |

No other edges: only one code epic exists, so no implementation-to-implementation
edges apply. There are no external dependencies, no new components requiring an
onboarding chain, and no open questions (the strategy states the audit report
enumerates the exact defects per flow), so no Investigation epics are needed.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Coverage |
|-----|----------|------|----------|
| HLR-1 (four core flows operable by keyboard, no focus traps or unreachable controls) | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Full |
| HLR-2 (visible, consistent focus indicators across audited flows) | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Full |
| HLR-3 (VPAT and accessibility statement updated and republished, with technical review) | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Full |

All HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Design Decisions

- **HLR-1 and HLR-2 bundled into one epic.** Both concern the same logical
  change (keyboard accessibility remediation of the four audited flows), on the
  same component, same team, and the same UI surfaces (modals and controls in
  those flows). Focus-trap fixes and focus-indicator consistency touch the same
  components; splitting them would make two epics modify the same UI surfaces
  independently.
- **E002 priority = P2** via the docs-authoring priority exception: the strategy
  frontmatter priority is Normal → P2. This matches HLR-3's own P2 priority;
  the docs epic does not push priority upstream to E001.
- **Documentation component mapping.** "Documentation" is a canonical RHAI
  component in `.context/rhai-components.txt` but has no architecture-context
  file. It is a content-process component, not a code component, so the
  appropriate routing is a `docs-authoring` epic rather than a
  repo/konflux onboarding chain (Rule 20 does not apply — nothing is being
  provisioned). The "RHOAI Documentation" team assignment is inferred; the
  strategy provides no Impacted Teams table (see Health Warnings).
- **Scope level.** Epic scope stays at the functional level of the strategy
  (keyboard operability, focus retention in modals, indicator consistency).
  Specific implementation techniques (focus-trap utilities, indicator styling
  approach) are left to the implementing team.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections.** The strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements section. The decomposition proceeded with
  available information; team assignments were taken from architecture context
  (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard) and inferred for Documentation.
- **Scope trap (mild).** HLR-3 requires a *published* conformance statement
  before customer renewal. Publication channels and review sign-off for a VPAT
  are a human process gate outside the code work; the docs epic carries an
  explicit technical-review AC, but the renewal deadline itself is a business
  commitment, not an engineering AC.
- **Out-of-scope boundary.** Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard
  fixes require and flows outside the four audited ones are explicitly out of
  scope; acceptance criteria below are scoped to the four audited flows only.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing. The single
dependency (docs after code) is internal to the strategy.
